title: Quality, reliability and engagement of aortic dissection-related health information on TikTok: a cross-sectional study from China
screen_reason: QUALITY-ONLY study with no share. The 151 Chinese-language TikTok videos on aortic dissection were scored only with the Global Quality Scale (GQS 1-5) and modified DISCERN (0-5), and the results are reported exclusively as medians with IQRs (median GQS 3 (IQR 2-4); median mDISCERN 2 (IQR 1-2)), plus regression coefficients. No video is ever classified as false, misleading, inaccurate or misinformation against any external ground truth, and no share of videos above or below any quality threshold is reported. Per §3 this is construct QUALITY, and per §1 a scale score reported only as a median/mean with no derivable share yields no row (R8: no complement, sum or threshold share may be computed).
missed_or_uncertain: (1) '92.72% of videos were uploaded by health professionals' (140/151 health professionals vs 11 non-health professionals) - a share of uploader type, not of misinformation; no row. (2) Median GQS 3 (IQR 2-4) and median mDISCERN 2 (IQR 1-2) overall, and by uploader type (health professionals GQS 3, mDISCERN 2; non-health professionals GQS 1, mDISCERN 1) - scale scores reported as medians only, no share of items, so no QUALITY row could be built (a QUALITY row needs a share; none is derivable without computing a threshold count that the paper never gives). (3) The Discussion quotes figures from OTHER papers that would be tempting but are cited from elsewhere and therefore barred by R8: 'Charl et al. found that only 53% of YouTube Aortic valve stenosis videos were of high educational value despite 74% originating from professional sources, with 47% rated as misleading or incomplete', plus physician-authorship shares of 22-68%, 75.1%, 85.6%, 94.6% and 92% from other studies. (4) Correlations and regression betas (likes/comments vs GQS/mDISCERN, the 'popularity paradox') are associations, not prevalence. (5) The word 'misinformation' appears in the framing and implications but is never operationalised or measured.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis. Keyword search ('aortic dissection') on TikTok/Douyin in mainland China, not logged in, videos published before 1 March 2026; the first 160 search results taken, minus 6 duplicates, 2 medical-insurance and 1 unrelated video, leaving 151. Two independent cardiovascular specialists scored every video on GQS and mDISCERN following a prespecified rubric; ICC(3,1) 0.902 (95% CI 0.868-0.928) for GQS and 0.852 (0.802-0.891) for mDISCERN; discrepancies adjudicated by a third senior specialist. Stated limitations: cross-sectional snapshot; search results depend on platform ranking (selection bias); uploader professional status self-reported and unverifiable; Chinese-language only; GQS and mDISCERN involve subjective judgement. Note the rank-truncated sampling (first 160 results) - had an eligible estimate existed it would have been denom_selection=curated, sampling_frame=keyword_topical, topic=health_other.
rob.item6_quote: Two independent cardiovascular specialists with extensive clinical experience evaluated all 151 eligible videos using the GQS [1-5] and the mDISCERN [0-5] instruments... the GQS (26) is a global 5-point measure of overall educational quality and usefulness, incorporating the coherence/flow and practicality of the health information, whereas mDISCERN (27) is a 5-item checklist that assesses the reliability of health information.
rob.item10_quote: Across the 151 videos, overall quality was moderate [median GQS: 3 (IQR, 2-4) and median mDISCERN: 2 (IQR, 1-2)].
